title: What must a handoff carry, and how does the swap happen?
context: Decision 10 retires an orchestrator past a context threshold and the new holder starts from the board plus a handoff memo. Today that memo is free text the outgoing agent writes from memory. The goal is that nothing in flight is lost and the next holder can carry on as if nothing changed.

options.name: A better memo
options.summary: Keep the agent-written memo, but require set headings in it: work in flight, promises to you, open questions, risks, next step.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='60' y='40' width='200' height='100' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='160' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Memo</text><text x='160' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>headings required</text></svg>
cons: The agent can still misremember who is doing what
Facts the hub already knows get retyped and can be wrong

options.name: Hub writes the facts, agent writes the judgement
options.summary: The hub fills in what it knows for certain: each worker and its last summary, open cards, decisions waiting, recent messages from you. The outgoing orchestrator writes only judgement under required headings: why things are the way they are, promises to you, risks, what it would do next, and board tidy-ups. The hub refuses a handoff that skips a heading and asks again. Workers follow the same rule at their own threshold.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='20' y='30' width='130' height='120' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='85' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Facts</text><text x='85' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>(from the hub)</text><rect x='170' y='30' width='130' height='120' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='235' y='87' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Judgement</text><text x='235' y='101' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>(from the agent)</text><text x='160' y='168' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>one handoff entry</text></svg>
pros: The agent spends its words on what only it knows
Same shape for orchestrators and workers
cons: The next holder cannot ask about anything left unclear

options.name: B, plus a short overlap
options.summary: As B, then the new orchestrator reads the handoff and may ask the outgoing one a few questions (say up to three, or ten minutes) before it retires. The questions and answers are saved with the handoff so later holders see them too.
options.sketch: <svg viewBox='0 0 320 180'><rect x='20' y='50' width='110' height='80' rx='6' fill='var(--muted)' fill-opacity='0.35' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='75' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Outgoing</text><rect x='190' y='50' width='110' height='80' rx='6' fill='var(--accent)' fill-opacity='0.85' stroke='currentColor'/><text x='245' y='94' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>Incoming</text><line x1='188' y1='75' x2='132' y2='75' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='132,75 138.3,72.0 138.3,78.0' fill='currentColor'/><line x1='132' y1='105' x2='188' y2='105' stroke='currentColor'/><polygon points='188,105 181.7,108.0 181.7,102.0' fill='currentColor'/><text x='160' y='68' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>asks</text><text x='160' y='125' font-size='11' text-anchor='middle' fill='currentColor'>answers</text></svg>
pros: Gaps get filled before the old agent is gone
The Q and A becomes part of the memory
cons: Two agents run briefly, so a little more of your plan
The outgoing agent is already near its limit, so answers should be short

recommendation: Splitting facts from judgement makes the handoff reliable; the short overlap is what makes it seamless, and it costs little because the questions are few and the answers short.

settles.value: hub writes the facts (workers, last summaries, open cards, waiting decisions); outgoing agent writes judgement under required headings; incoming agent may ask the outgoing one up to three questions before it retires; same rule for workers
